subject: CTO availability conflict — request to nudge demo by 45 minutes
messages:
From: Dana Romero <dana@skylinedata.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CTO asked to join — can we nudge the demo later by ~45m?

Hi Markus / Lauren,

Quick note — our CTO (Arun Patel) just confirmed he'd like to join the demo but his previous meeting is running into airport check-in. He has a short window from 11:30–12:15 PT before boarding. The current demo is set for 11:00–12:00 PT, so he'd miss the first half.

Would Redwood be able to shift the slot 45 minutes later so Arun can see the key architecture section and the Q&A? If moving the full demo isn't possible, would you consider doing a short 20–25 minute CTO-focused walkthrough + then handing off to the broader session? We want Arun to personally see the latency / routing and security slides.

We're flexible on format — compressed CTO run-through or shift the whole 11:00 slot to 11:45. Please advise what would be least disruptive for your team.

Thanks,
Dana Romero
Director of Product 
Skyline Data, Inc.
+1 415-555-0198

P.S. attaching the agenda we use internally so you can see the sections Arun wants (security + routing + cost controls).

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Dana Romero <dana@skylinedata.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CTO asked to join — can we nudge the demo later by ~45m?

Hi Dana — thanks for the heads-up and the agenda (received). Happy to accommodate Arun; we have two practical options:

1) Shift the entire demo to 11:45–12:45 PT. That keeps the full flow intact (intro → architecture → demo → Q&A) but pushes our post-demo debrief.
2) Keep 11:00 start; run a 25-minute focused CTO briefing at 11:30 (security + routing + cost controls) and then transition to the broader demo for the rest — effectively compressing the first half.

Option 1 is cleaner for us operationally but requires attendees on our side to move by 45 minutes. Option 2 minimizes attendee movement but compresses some sections. If you confirm Option 1, Lauren/Rishi and I will update invites and runbooks.

We also have an internal standby (Rishi) who can lead the architecture/system deep-dive if I need to join another brief at 12:15.

Tell me which you prefer and I'll action immediately.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

---

Markus / Rishi — forwarding Dana's note after checking calendars. Quick internal call notes below before we reply to confirm: 

- Option 1 (shift full meeting to 11:45): I checked the AE and SE calendars — AE (Kayla) can move, SE (Rishi) can also move but there is a downstream call at 13:00 that Rishi is leading. We can cover it by swapping Rishi out for me for the last 20 minutes.
- Option 2 (compressed CTO briefing): Low disruption but we lose a small demo scenario (cost routing sim). We could record that sim and share post-demo with Arun.

Recommendation: Shift the full meeting to 11:45–12:45 PT. Reason: Arun asked to see the live architecture portion; compressing risks not letting him ask follow-ups. We'll adjust internal runbook: Rishi covers architecture 11:45–12:15; Markus joins 12:15–12:45 for Q&A and product value discussion. If anything changes, we keep the compressed path as fallback.

I'll update the calendar + meeting invite now and add a short note about attendee swaps. Markus — please send a quick confirmation to Dana and include the updated calendar link.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
